title: What If a Cosmic Ray Flipped One Bit in a Computer?

scenes.text: What if a cosmic ray flipped one bit in a computer? It may have once changed an election.
In May 2003, a Belgian town counted electronic votes. One party's tally came out 4,096 votes too high.
Officials caught it because that party had more preferential votes than votes for its own list, which is impossible.
The number is the clue. 4,096 is two to the power of twelve, exactly what one flipped bit adds.
The government blamed a bit that appeared spontaneously in memory. One explanation is a cosmic ray hitting the chip.
Smaller chips need less energy to hold a bit, so it takes less radiation to flip one. When the count was rerun, every other number matched.
